# Pending changes (since patch 0008, 2026-11-09)

## 2026-11-09 - Live coding: LiveLink, hot reload, a debugger, the developer menu and the Inspector
**Asked:** "how could you expose the game live state so we can do a completely live coding workflow" -> yes;
then "add also hot reloading and live debugging"; then "alt + right click should open a developer menu,
one entry will be the inspector - a window to the right of the main window that displays values of live objects".

**Done:**
- **LiveLink** (scripts/live_link.gd, new autoload): off unless a debug run is started with the user arg
  `--live[=PORT]`; then a TCP server on 127.0.0.1:6070 (this machine only), one JSON command per line:
  ping, state (ship / signal site and level / enemies by distance / fps), eval (Expression - names main,
  ship, site, root, tree, live, every autoload, Engine/Input/OS/Time/DisplayServer...), set (indexed
  property paths), run (GDScript statements compiled into a throwaway script's run(), may await), reload,
  watch, events (a log fed by an OS Logger: prints, errors with their script line, reloads), tree, shot,
  pause, speed, inspect.
- **Hot reload:** GDScript.reload(keep_state) - live objects keep their values and get the new code; loaded
  scripts that extend a changed one reload after it (base first: reloading space_monster.gd reloads all 10
  creature scripts under a live Hydra); the new source is first compiled on the side (class_name blanked)
  so broken code is reported (with its real file:line) and the old code keeps running; shaders get their
  new code (every material updates), other loaded resources reload in place. A file watcher (every 0.5 s:
  scripts, shaders, data - .gd/.gdshader/.png/.json) does it automatically (on with --live; menu toggle).
  LiveLink never reloads itself (that hung the game in testing).
- **The debugger** (external/live_debugger/: a tiny separate Godot project, so Godot does its own
  message encoding): `python3 tools/live.py debugger` runs a remote-debugger server the game connects to
  (`--remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:6007`), driven on port 6071: breakpoints (sent again on reconnect),
  pause/step/next/out/continue, the stack, a frame's locals/members/globals, evaluate in a frame,
  output/errors with their call stacks, Godot's own reload_scripts. Script errors don't stop the game by
  default (`dbg errors on` to break on them) - a game nobody is watching would freeze.
- **tools/live.py:** the command line for both (state, eval, set, run [-f file], reload, hot on|off,
  shot, pause, speed, inspect, log [--follow]; dbg status/events/break/clear/pause/step/next/out/
  continue/stack/vars/eval/reload/errors).
- **Developer menu** (any debug run): Alt + right-click (LiveLink._input, before Main's right-click scanner)
  -> Inspect <the world object under the cursor> (nearest scripted Node2D within its click radius or 40
  screen px) / Inspect UI <hovered control>, Inspector, Pause, Game speed (x0.25-x4), Hot reload, Screenshot.
- **The Inspector** (scripts/dev_inspector.gd): a native OS window (force_native - set while hidden, or
  Godot ignores it) placed right of the game's window (560 px wide, the game's height; inside the screen
  if there's no room). Node tree (lazy: two levels, more as opened; filter; opens the way to the inspected
  node), properties (script variables, + built-in), refreshed 5x a second, arrays/dicts/objects expand,
  double-click an object to inspect it (Back), edit numbers/strings/bools/vectors/colours in place.
  Made-up node names (@Node2D@494) show the object's display_name / type_id instead ("The Hydra (@Node2D@494)").
- **Tests:** tests/test_live.gd (6): off unless asked, eval/set/run, hot reload keeps state + broken code
  keeps the old, the file watcher, the TCP door, the Inspector's value parsing/editing. The test runner
  gained `expect_errors` (TestCase): engine errors a test causes on purpose aren't failures.
- **Docs:** data/docs/editor.md - a new chapter "Developer tools" (dev-menu, live-coding); test expects 9 chapters.

**Numbers:** LiveLink ~720 lines, Inspector ~520, debugger daemon ~340, live.py ~190. Hydra live: state
in one call; breakpoint at hydra_beast.gd:177 hit within a frame; eval `length * 2` = 920 in the frame;
65 fps after continuing. Probe object: count 72 -> 10076 across a reload (state kept, new code at once).

**Files:** scripts/live_link.gd (new), scripts/dev_inspector.gd (new), project.godot (autoload),
external/live_debugger/{project.godot,debugger.gd} (new), tools/live.py (new), tests/test_live.gd (new),
tests/test_case.gd, tests/run_tests.gd, tests/test_editor.gd, data/docs/editor.md.

## 2026-11-09 - The Library: no plate's text over another's
**Asked:** "in the library no asset's text should overlap with another asset's text".

**Done:** measured every room (external/playtests/library_overlaps.gd - each room's plates, the text rects
that overlap, and a whole-room screenshot): Buildings had 13 overlapping pairs (tile / decor names wider
than their 56-unit spacing), Monsters 18 (each creature's description laid out ~4800 world units wide at

## 2026-11-09 - The Inspector: reset to defaults (+ hot reload fixes found doing it)
**Asked:** "i want reset buttons in the inspector that will reset fields to their default values".

**Done:**
- Each property row whose value isn't its default gets a reset button (the editor's undo icon, ↺, tooltip
  "Reset to the default: <value>"); **Reset all** (in the header beside Built-in) resets every such field.
  Defaults: built-in properties - ClassDB's engine default; script variables - the declared value, read from
  the source (its own and its base scripts'): each top-level `var x := <value>` / `var x: T = <value>`
  (exported or not), the value evaluated as an Expression with the script's constants (literals, vectors,
  colours, arrays, dictionaries, maths) - nothing of the game runs. (Godot's
  Script.get_property_default_value only knows @export variables: 2 of the ship's; the source gives 32.)
  Values worked out at run time (`var hull := max_hull`, @onready) and objects have no default, no button.
  Arrays / dictionaries reset to a deep copy (not the script's own).
- The reset controls are made lazily (in _process), so an Inspector already open gets them when its script
  is hot reloaded - which is how they first appeared, live, in the user's running playtest.
- **Hot reload fix:** variables a reload adds were null in objects that already existed (the open Inspector's
  new `_defaults` was null -> ~19,000 errors in a few minutes). LiveLink now gives added variables their
  declared defaults in every node whose script is (or extends) the reloaded one (event "gave N new variable(s)
  ... their defaults"). Note: a typed Dictionary var holding nothing doesn't compare == null - check typeof.
- **Inspector fix:** opening a row filled it inside the Tree's own item_collapsed signal - once returned a null
  item (an error in the user's session); now deferred, and guarded.
- **Log fix:** the events reply was cut at 500 entries by jsonable (the oldest 500, ending in a string that
  crashed `live.py log`); now the latest 400, and live.py skips anything that isn't an event.
- Tests: test_live.gd 8 (+ reset to defaults: declared / engine / computed-has-none / constants / reset all /
  array copy / buttons only on changed rows; + a reload gives new variables their defaults).
- Docs: editor.md dev-menu (reset buttons, Reset all), hot reload (new variables get their declared values).

**Files:** scripts/dev_inspector.gd, scripts/live_link.gd, tools/live.py, tests/test_live.gd, data/docs/editor.md.

Also: full suite 117/118 - test_play.test_followed_ships_fly_steady flaky under load (failed, then passed on rerun
with the user's game running alongside); unrelated to these changes.

under its title bar, 8 px margins), after that where it was left (kept on screen if the game's window shrank);

## 2026-11-09 - The Inspector snaps to the game window's edges
**Asked:** "make sure the inspector window can snap to the game window edges".

**Done:** DevInspector.snap() every frame: comparing its rect with last frame's - moved (title bar): any frame edge
within 24 px of a game window edge snaps flush (left/right, top/bottom, so corners too); resized (an edge): only
the edges that moved snap (the others stay); the game window resized: docked edges follow it (docked on both sides:
it stretches). The frame is Godot's embedded window frame (embedded_border's expand margins: 8 / 32 with the title
bar / 8 / 8), so it's the drawn frame that goes flush, not the content. Snapping is magnetic: Godot sets the position
from the mouse on every drag motion, so moving on past 24 px unsticks it. First open: docked right, top to bottom.
Test: test_inspector_snaps_to_edges (each edge, free in the middle, resize, corner, the game window resized).
(In the running playtest - still the old LiveLink - the new variables arrived null again while the user was
resizing it; set by hand. New launches get them via LiveLink's new-variable defaults.)

**Files:** scripts/dev_inspector.gd, tests/test_live.gd, data/docs/editor.md.

## 2026-11-09 - Fix: the developer menu after using the Inspector
**Reported:** after clicking in the Inspector, Alt + right-click on the game did nothing - until a left click (moving
the ship) on the game.

**Cause:** a focused embedded window gets every mouse click, even outside it; only a left click outside takes the focus
back (Godot's Viewport._sub_windows_forward_input). So the Alt + right-click went to the Inspector, never reaching
LiveLink._input on the game's viewport.

**Fix:** DevInspector._input catches Alt + right-click while it has focus and opens the developer menu at the click
(its local position + its own position = the game view's coordinates). Also: the menu's popup origin is now chosen by
whether the game's viewport embeds subwindows (an embedded menu: view coordinates; a native one: + the window's screen
position) - `is_embedded()` asked before the menu was ever shown could add the window's screen position (y = 1020 in the
user's playtests) and put the menu off the window. Test test_menu_after_using_the_inspector (Input.parse_input_event -
the same path as a real click; window pixels via the root's final transform - headless stretches a 64 px window to a
1920 view). The running playtest: reloaded, and set_process_input(true) by hand (Godot enables _input at ready only).

**Files:** scripts/dev_inspector.gd, scripts/live_link.gd, tests/test_live.gd.

## 2026-11-09 - Many more signals: 12-36 per system (and what it took to keep 60 fps)
**Asked:** "i want many more signals per solar system, something between 12 to 36".

**Done:**
- SignalSites.generate: COUNT 12-36 a system each epoch (was 3-4): every kind at least once (the first six,
  shuffled), then kinds at random; RING 4,000-16,000 from the star (was 4,500-12,500) and APART >= 1,500 from each
  other (40 tries per signal). Same seed -> same set. Galaxy.signals_in keeps up to 12 located-unfinished signals
  into a new epoch (was 3). Live: Atrapos regenerated in the user's playtest - 34 signals (9 distress calls,
  8 debris fields, 7 creatures, 5 combat, 3 hazard fields, 2 anomalies).
- **Performance** (measured live with LiveLink, play_space.gd at 1600x900): with 34 located signals the frame's
  script time went 18 -> 37 ms (60 -> ~38 fps), and a scan's 34 paths held it at 25 ms all scan long. Fixed:
  - SignalBeacon redraws only when on screen (its rings and label, 400 px round the view) - 34 beacons cost ~11 ms
    a frame redrawing off screen; now 20 ms with 34 located (18 with none).
  - Scan paths (ShipScanner._draw_paths): only the stretches of each path crossing the view are drawn
    (_draw_path_run per run of on-screen segments; pulses and destination rings only on screen), 4 glow layers
    (GLOW, was 6) not antialiased, 12-40 samples a path (was 16-160), the curve inlined, colour arrays filled in
    place. Whole scan with 34 paths: 16.7 ms every half second sampled (vsync 60) - was 25 ms.
- Tests: test_signals_generated - 12-36, every kind, none closer than APART, counts vary over 40 systems/epochs.
  Docs: game.md "12 to 36 at a time (every kind among them)".
- New: external/playtests/play_space.gd (a new game straight into space - for measuring / live coding).

**Files:** scripts/signal_sites.gd, scripts/galaxy.gd, scripts/signal_beacon.gd, scripts/ship_scanner.gd,
tests/test_signals.gd, data/docs/game.md, external/playtests/play_space.gd (new).

## 2026-11-09 - Fix: LiveLink `run` crashed the game (double free)
Found while measuring: a second `live.py run` snippet that made lambdas (`.filter(func ...)`) crashed Godot 4.7
("double free or corruption") - freeing the throwaway script whose code had made lambdas. Reproduced headless
(2nd run). LiveLink now keeps every snippet's script and object for the whole run (_runs); 25 runs in a row fine.
Test test_run_snippets_with_lambdas (8 runs). (The user's running playtest still has the old LiveLink - no lambdas
in snippets there until its next launch.)

**Files:** scripts/live_link.gd, tests/test_live.gd.

## 2026-11-09 - Buildings hot reload (tile pictures, tile sheets, building styles)
**Asked:** "make sure building can be hot reloaded when i change the graphics or extend them".

**Done:**
- Every building sprite made from the Minoan pieces is tagged with how it was made (MinoanTiles.tag, meta "minoan_skin"):
  walls [orient, kind, variant, style], roof tiles, upper-floor floor / roof tiles (building_floors.gd), crown pieces
  (caps / antenna / dome / horns), columns and entrance pieces [style, role, index, height], decor [style, the rng roll];
  the floor TileSetAtlasSources are kept in PlanetSurface._minoan_floors. MinoanTiles.reskin(root, floors) gives each
  its texture again from the current pieces and STYLES - the building's shape, doors, rooms, stairs, furniture and
  walking stay as they are (no rebuild).
- MinoanTiles.hot_reload(changed): those pieces are read from their PNGs from then on (a running game can't re-import;
  ImageTextures with mipmaps), composed walls / floors are redone. Pieces with no import yet (added while it runs) are
  read from their PNGs too (_from_file) - extending works before an import.
- LiveLink: watches data/sprites (and reports new files, not only changed ones); a changed tile_*.png or a reloaded
  minoan_tiles.gd -> hot_reload + reskin_buildings() on group "hot_buildings" (PlanetSurface; the Library rebuilds its
  Buildings room). A changed external/images/*tile_sheet*.png is cut again on a thread (python3 tools/extract_sprites.py
  <sheet>) and its pieces come in like any changed picture. eval now knows the game's class_name scripts.
- Measured live on Thalassa (external/playtests/play_surface.gd, new): tinting the palace's stone wall PNGs green ->
  "buildings: 2 tile picture(s) - 2010 piece(s) redone" within the 0.5 s scan; the extra sheet touched -> cut (58
  pieces, ~12 s) -> reloaded -> redone; a piece added to the warehouse decor in STYLES -> "and the styles - 2010 piece(s)
  redone" (both reverted).
- Tests: test_surface test_buildings_hot_reload (tags on walls / roofs / pieces / decor / floors, a wall's picture
  changed shows on the building, LiveLink's path, back again); test_live test_eval_knows_the_game_classes. Docs: editor.md.

## 2026-11-09 - Rugged Greek terrain, one body of water, solid crags
**Asked:** "too many bodies of water, even the most green map should have a lake or a river, or a plain coast line,
dont put pools of water all over the map, also the surface terrain is too flat, use geography of Greece to emulate
similar rocky uneven terrain, make sure that collisions with the uneven terrain work correctly".

**Done:**
- New scripts/surface_terrain.gd (SurfaceTerrain, preloaded as PlanetSurface.TERRAIN; worker thread, static): the
  height map is no longer one noise thresholded into land and water (which made pools everywhere). Instead:
  - **Relief** after Greece: ridged simplex (5 octaves, domain-warped: mountain crests) + rolling hills, normalised,
    curved (r^1.7: wide lowlands, steep mountains).
  - **One body of water** - pdata "water": "coast" (a wavy coastline along one side, ~17% sea, 2-4 islets off it),
    "lake" (one noisy ellipse 18-30 tiles), "river" (meandering across the map, 5-9 tiles wide, passing the landing
    site at 0.2-0.28 N, 3 raised fords / ice bridges 6 tiles wide) or "none". Thalassa: coast; Krystallos: river (a
    crevasse); Selene: none (no unwalkable ground). Default: picked by seed. A signed distance to the water drives the
    heights: water deepens over 10 tiles (shallows then deep), land rises from the shore over 14 (beach band first).
  - **Crags** (rock bytes 0..255 per tile): along the ridge crests and in outcrop patches on high ground, away from water
    and the landing site; a morphological closing (Chebyshev r 2) fills gullies / nooks narrower than ~5 tiles.
  - Thalassa: 17% sea, 52% grassland, 29% forest (forest threshold 0.22 -> 0.3), 4.4% crags; Selene 3.9%; Krystallos
    1.7% crevasse, 4.6% crags. Generation 0.3-0.56 s (headless).
- **Ground texture** L8 -> RGF: R height, G rock (exact floats). shaders/ground.gdshader: broad hillshade from the height
  map (light from the upper left, +-30%), high ground paler; crags drawn from the same rock bytes - a limestone top
  (cracks, bevel lit from the upper left, bright lip) and a 46 px cliff face below it (fissures, strata, darker toward
  the foot), a shadow at the foot, scree round it. rock_color uniform (pdata "rock_color"; Selene grey, Krystallos
  blue-grey ice rock). The shader's edge noise no longer moves a shoreline: where it would flip walkable/unwalkable the
  plain filtered height is used - shores drawn exactly where the game's walkability is (it wasn't before: a ford drawn
  as crevasse was walkable).
- **Collisions:** PlanetSurface._ground_ok blocks where the bilinear rock (SurfaceTerrain.rock_interp - the shader's
  filtering) >= 0.5, and the cliff face (the point 46 px above is a crag top) - so the path grid, walking, NPCs and
  flora placement all see exactly what's drawn. walkable_cell / _cell_walkable_h (villages, gates, pirates) skip crag
  tiles. _connect_islands counts crags (with a margin, and their faces) as solid; small patches hemmed in by crags
  become crag (_rock_pocket, POCKET 40); causeways cut passes through crags (_clear_rock). Building plots, the landing
  site, village centres and gates are cleared of crags (_clear_site, _add_clear_spot). Painting terrain in the level
  editor removes crags under the brush.
  Checked: a pilot walking 700 px straight through a crag (half the straight line blocked) went round it, 0 frames in
  rock; everything reachable on all three planets (a 3-tile nook was unreachable before the closing).
- Flora: nothing grows on scree (rock >= 30): boulders and rocks there instead (half the tiles); forest is open
  woodland (a tree on 45% of tiles, bushes, some rocks) - was 1-2 trees per tile.
- The planet map shows crags pale (rock >= 128) and scree.

**Note:** the user's playtest crashed while I edited planet_surface.gd: LiveLink hot-reloaded the running surface with

member variables of a live object is beyond what hot reload can carry - restart the game after such changes.

## 2026-11-09 - Real elevation: the ground stands up
**Asked:** "terrain still is flat" (after the Greek relief above - hillshading alone didn't read as height).

**Done:**
- The ground is a mesh now (was one flat Polygon2D): a vertex at every tile corner (441 x 441 = 194,481 vertices,
  387,200 triangles, built on the worker thread - SurfaceTerrain.ground_mesh), its triangles ordered back to front
  (by i + j) so nearer hills are drawn over the land behind. shaders/ground.gdshader's vertex() lifts each vertex by
  the elevation; the fragment still works in ground-plane coordinates (wpos = the unlifted vertex).
- SurfaceTerrain.elevation (the shader computes the same): ELEV_K 680 px per unit of height above the site height
  (what plots are levelled to: buildings, floors and the landing pad stay at 0 - nothing in them needed lifting),
  water flat at its level (max(h, water_top)), crags + CRAG_H 72 px from the solid line (rock 0.4) to 0.7 - real
  cliffs (the crag face texture now on that steep rise; the old painted 46 px face and its collision offset are gone),
  easing over RIM 10 tiles to the rim's level (the cube's brick sides moved to it). Mountains on Thalassa stand ~340 px.
- Rocky, uneven ground: knolls and hollows (noise 0.07, amplitude 0.035 + 0.05 x relief) on the land; hillshade
  sharper (1-tile slopes, x9).
- Everything standing on the ground is drawn lifted, its position staying on the ground plane (all game logic,
  walking, paths, collisions unchanged): PlanetSurface._apply_lifts on RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw moves the
  canvas item of each node in group "surface_lift" (Thing and all its kinds - NPCs, pirates, gates, loot, furniture -
  the Pilot, laser bolts, arrows) up by lift_at(position); scenery is lifted once when made (_lift_static; ground
  cover: PropData.lift in the batch). The camera's offset follows the drawn pilot.
- Mouse: screen_to_ground - a ray down the screen column, from the front: the first ground point drawn at or above the
  cursor, bisected - the front-most where hills overlap (round trip within 22 px, the rest being points hidden behind
  nearer ground). Clicking / holding to walk use it; clicking things and enemies compares with where they're drawn.
- The landing site levelled to the site height (_level_disc, 9 tiles + 14 easing); plots ramp into the land over
  PLOT_EASE 10 tiles (was 2), and villages prefer sites near the site height (cost |h - site_h| x 6).
- Crag thresholds aligned to the new solid line (closing at rock >= 102, crag tiles >= 90).
60 fps on the surface (1920 x 1080, RTX 2070).

**Files:** scripts/surface_terrain.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/surface_props.gd,
shaders/ground.gdshader, data/docs/game.md.

## 2026-11-09 - Terraced Greek terrain (the reference image), and no shooting through walls
**Asked:** a reference image (~/Downloads/96a645cc-...png: Greek coast, limestone terraces and cliffs, olive and
cypress trees, sea and islands) - "this is how I want the terrain to look and behave"; "make sure npcs cannot shoot
through walls".

**Done - terrain:**
- Ledges (SurfaceTerrain.terrace): elevation = STEP 110 px per TERRACE 0.2 of height, each ledge nearly flat (15% tilt)
  then a sheer drop over its last CLIFF_W 12% - a cliff where the land climbs fast, a gentle slope where it climbs
  slowly. `ramp` (0..1 per tile, blurred: _blur_ramp) turns drops into walkable slopes: about half the land by nature
  (noise), and always round plots, the landing site, village centres, gates, shores (beaches and banks), and ramps cut
  to cut-off ledges (_carve_causeway). The site height sits at a ledge's foot: buildings at elevation 0, ramp or not.
- Elevation is computed continuously (the filtered height, ramp, crags -> ledges) by both the shader and lift_at, so
  cliffs follow the land's contours, not the tile grid. The ground texture is RGBAF: height, solid rock, ramp, crags.
- A fine ground mesh round the camera (FINE_W 100 tiles, FINE_SUB 4 x 4 quads a tile = 160,801 vertices, placed by the
  shader from win_origin, never culled) over the coarse whole-map mesh (which leaves the window out): crisp cliffs.
  The slope is computed per vertex (varying), not per pixel: 60 fps (39 with per-pixel).
- Cliff faces drawn in screen space (spos) as limestone courses - blocks with joints, sunlit tops, cracks, stains -
  warm pinkish limestone (ROCK_COLOR 0.8, 0.7, 0.62); Thalassa's grass warmer, Greek (0.52, 0.62, 0.28).
- Collision: a cliff is where the ground climbs CLIFF_PX 22 px a tile or more (and isn't a ramp) - _ground_ok tests
  exactly that near a cliff (_on_cliff: 3 elevations), the shader draws walls exactly there. Checked over 40,000 points
  round the landing site: 0 points drawn as wall are walkable (test_cliffs_block_where_drawn, all 3 planets).
  Per tile, _mark_cliffs flags the tiles a drop crosses (_cliff, used by villages, scenery, maps: _solid);
  reachability (_walk_open) keeps a tile clear of cliffs (the path grid does); cut-off ledges are linked by a ramp
  (within MAX_CAUSEWAY 60 tiles, one sweep from the main land: _sweep_from) or filled in (_rock_pocket,
  _fill_unreached); NPCs planned onto a cliff are moved off it.
- Build times: Thalassa 7.4 s, Selene 10.8 s, Krystallos 7.4 s (Selene took 350 s while every one of its 1,241 cut-off
  patches got a long ramp - now about half the land is natural slope).
- (Before the ledges, two steps on the way: elevation from a smooth height x 680 px - "still flat" - and the shader's
  painted cliff faces.)

**Done - walls:** PlanetSurface.shot_clear(a, b): no building wall segment across the line (doorways are gaps) and no
crag / cliff along it. NPCs pick only targets they can see (MinoanNpc._foe, SurfacePirate._target), hold fire without
a clear line (gunner, pirate, archer); your own rifle too (Pilot.fire_at) - you walk round until you can see your
target. Laser bolts and arrows burst on a wall or rock face in their path (checked each frame on the ground under
them). test_no_shooting_through_walls.

**Also:** tests/run_tests.gd takes a second filter, for test names: `-- test_surface cliffs`.

## 2026-11-10 - You fight back against animals

**Reported:** "i cannot attack creatures at all, even though they can attack me".

**Why:** clicking a predator (or F) did attack it, as a test and a scripted click in the game showed. But a
pack bites from all sides, overlapping your pilot, and it took a fresh click per animal. After the first kill
the pilot stood still while the rest of the pack bit, so it felt like you couldn't fight back.

**Done:**
- Firing back: whatever bit you in the last 1.5 s (`bitten_by_node`) becomes the pilot's trigger when you
  aren't fighting anyone. You shoot it while still free to walk or run, until it falls or you're out of reach
  (`PlanetSurface._fire_back`).
- On to the next: when the enemy you attacked falls, you attack the nearest hostile within reach that's after
  you, either a beast hunting you or a pirate aiming at you (`_next_attacker`).
- `Pilot.fire_at` stops at a fallen enemy. It used to keep shooting at one still fading out.
- In a bot game, a pack of 3 wolves is beaten in about 3 s with no clicks (the pilot ends at 75 health).
- Tests: test_you_can_kill_a_predator (click a boar, snake or wolf and it falls) and test_you_fire_back_at_a_pack.
- game.md's Wildlife entry is updated.

tests/test_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md.

## 2026-11-10 - Hunting, Cybernetic Matter, a food chain and twice the animals

**Asked:** "i should be able also to attack any creatures, creatures also drop cybernetic matter, increase the
density of the population of creatures, allow them to attack each other and attack back".

**Done:**
- **Attack any animal:**
  - `PlanetSurface._targets()` returns the enemies plus every animal. `_hostile_at` uses it, with a
    hit box sized to the animal and raised for fliers.
  - `_update_attack` accepts any animal. `_next_attacker` includes animals coming for you.
  - F and the minimap still mean real enemies only, and the guards don't shoot sheep. Peaceful animals left
    `_thing_at`: clicking one now attacks it.
  - Health bars show on any hurt animal. Laser bolts aim at a flier's height (`LaserBolt._aim_point`).
- **Cybernetic Matter:** a new cargo item, `cyber_matter` (value 30, circuit-node icon). Every fallen animal
  leaves a LootDrop chest with a cyan light, holding 1 to 8 matter (max_hp / 20). LootDrop now has a
  label and a light colour.
- **Density:** `SurfaceCreature.DENSITY` 2 doubles every planet's groups. Thalassa has about 92 animals out
  around the pad, at about 0.2 ms a frame for 36 animals.
- **Fighting back:** big grazers ("fights" plus bite stats) turn on whoever hurts them: goat, deer, donkey,
  tigrokeros, mykelephas (charges), selas, scarab, rhinobeetle (charges), icestag. They run once badly hurt.
- **Food chain:**
  - A predator gets hungry 8–45 s after appearing, and again 40–90 s after feeding.
  - It hunts the nearest animal of another kind within sense that is on the ground and has no more health
    than itself. Its pack joins in, and after a kill it feeds (act pose, 3 s).
  - The hunted react through `spotted()`: grazers and skittish ones run, slow ones hide, birds fly off.
  - When bitten, a predator or a fighting grazer fights back (`attacked_by`).
- The chase and bite code moved to a shared `_fight()`, used by predators and by grazers that fight.

**Asked:** "i see pathfinding issue on Krystallos, make sure pathfinding works correctly, also add inventory and
toolbar for player and a tab menu similar to the tab menu of the spaceship".

**Pathfinding:**
- **Cause:** on tiled ground, a ledge whose ground drops away behind it (the far side, from the camera) had no
  visible edge. Its cliff faces away from you, and snow on snow (or grass on grass) looks flat. The pilot
  walked long ways round to a ramp past cliffs you couldn't see. The pathfinding was right, but the ground hid
  why.
  - Fix: TerrainTiles.RIMS. Rim pieces (rim_l, rim_r, rim_lr) are the base ground with a dark lip and a light
    line drawn along the back edge(s). `_tile_cells` uses them on flat tiles whose back neighbour (grid -x,
    -y) is lower land.
  - Krystallos has about 6,000 such ledge tiles, now drawn.
- **Walks stopping short:** a walk whose way round leaves the path grid's window (96 tiles around you) got a
  partial path and stopped at its end.
  - Fix: `_walk_to` now treats that as a far goal and goes on when the window moves.
  - Fix: a far goal stopped short with the window not caught up re-centres the window on you, or gives up
    cleanly when already centred (before, it could wait forever).
- **New test file tests/test_paths.gd:** 40 random walks per planet that have a way there must arrive,
  including doors and leg-by-leg walks. Krystallos, Selene and Thalassa: 120 of 120 arrive. Its tests run
  one per process (tools/test.py GROUP).

  SurfaceMap).
- Keys: 1-5 switch tabs, I opens the inventory, M the map, Tab closes. It closes when you're hit.
- M now opens the map; Tab used to open it.
- **Inventory:** the pilot's portrait, health, rifle stats (rate shown with overcharge), credits and every
  carried item (state player items). Hovering an item shows details; clicking medicine or an energy cell

- **Bestiary:** the planet's species (FAUNA) in 4 columns: picture, temper, health and bite, and hunted count.

  - Stored in state["player"]["bestiary"].

- 1 Laser rifle: attacks the nearest enemy, like F.
- 2 Medicine: +50 health, uses 1, 2 s cooldown.
- 3 Energy cell: the rifle fires twice as fast for 10 s (`Pilot.fire_every`), uses 1, 20 s cooldown.

## 2026-11-10 - Animals don't get stuck in corners

**Reported:** "i see some creatures get stuck in corners".

**Why:** animals walked straight at their goal, only trying a few angles left and right when blocked. In a
concave corner (a building's walls, a cliff bend) every one of those angles was blocked. A grazer kept picking
goals behind the wall, a chaser pushed into it forever, and a fleeing animal ran straight away from the threat
into the wall.

**Done (SurfaceCreature):**
- `_go_toward`: straight when the way is open (a segment check every 0.5 s), else along a route from the surface's
  path grid round the obstacle (re-planned every 0.8 s as the target moves). Wandering and chasing use it.
- `_open_spot`: wander goals near home that can be walked to in a straight line (8 tries, else home).
- `_run_from`: fleeing takes the open way, of 12 directions checked 120 px out, that leads furthest from the
  threat, re-chosen every 0.5 s.
- `_stuck`: no headway (under a quarter of its speed) for 1.5 s while walking makes it pick something else. A
  chaser stuck for 4 s gives up and goes home. It resets on every change of state.
- Test test_creatures_get_out_of_corners: a sheep set down hard against a building wanders off and is never
  pressed into a wall for long, and a wolf behind a building comes round it to you.

**Files:** scripts/surface_creature.gd, tests/test_surface.gd.
- Cost: about 1.5 ms a frame for the roughly 90 animals out near Thalassa's pad, mostly village herds stepping
  beside the walls.

## 2026-11-10 - Planet surfaces at 60 FPS and more

**Asked:** "optimise code makes sure planets render at least 60 FPS".

**Measured first** (bot game, 1600 x 900, vsync off, RTX 2070 Super - the scripts are in external/live_scripts/):

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Thalassa, landing pad (92 animals out) | 88 FPS, 11.1 ms | 150 FPS, 6.7 ms |
| Thalassa, dense forest | 102 FPS, 9.7 ms | - |
| Krystallos, landing pad | 134 FPS, 7.6 ms | 168 FPS, 5.6 ms |
| Draw calls / objects drawn (Thalassa pad) | 3,927 / 17,072 | 1,287 / 4,281 |
| Worst frame in a 20 s walk on Thalassa | 104 ms (5 frames over 25 ms) | 25 ms (1 frame) |

With vsync on at 60 Hz that leaves about 2.5x headroom at 1920 x 1080.

**Done:**
- **Ground tiles in two layers a level** (`_tile_cells`, `_build_tile_ground`): the flat tiles in an unsorted
  TileMapLayer, which the renderer batches by quadrant, and only the blocks and ramps y-sorted over them
  (their faces hang over the tiles in front). Before, every level's whole layer was y-sorted: a canvas item
  per tile. Draw calls fell by two thirds, objects drawn by three quarters.
- **Animal path searches** (the walking stalls): an animal routing round an obstacle to an unreachable spot
  (prey across water) made the A* explore the whole 384 x 384 grid - tens of ms in one frame, on Thalassa
  with 90 animals about. Now:
  - The path grid's worker labels every free point's region (a flood fill, `_make_nav`); `find_path(from,
    to, partial := false)` refuses a target in another region at once. The pilot keeps partial routes
    (a click on water walks you to the shore).
  - At most CREATURE_PATHS (2) animal searches a frame, shared between all of them.
  - `path_calls` / `path_us` count the searches for profiling.
- **Far animals think less often** (SurfaceCreature.FAR 1500 px, FAR_EVERY 4): beyond the screen an animal
  runs its behaviour every 4th frame with the time in between - the same behaviour, a quarter of the cost.
  About 70 of the 90 animals out are far. Creature scripts: 3.3 ms -> 2.2 ms a frame at the pad.
- **Minimap** redrawn 15 times a second instead of every frame (its draw costs about 0.9 ms).
- Fixed on the way: a hemmed-in animal (a building's inside corner) now picks the open way out nearest its
  home (`_open_spot`); test_creatures_get_out_of_corners judges wall-pressing over 40 s instead of a strolling
  distance that a slow grazer could miss by idling.
- Profiling scripts kept in external/live_scripts/ (perf_fps, perf_attrib, perf_walk_spikes - run with
  `python3 tools/live.py run -f <file>` in a live game).

**Files:** scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/surface_creature.gd, scripts/surface_minimap.gd, tests/test_surface.gd,
external/live_scripts/ (new).
- The region labelling is `_label_regions` (static, no allocations in the loop): 62 ms of the path grid's
  81 ms build, on its worker thread - the grid arrives about 60 ms later after each window shift. A first,
  allocating version took long enough that test_walk_into_and_out_of_buildings (which drives frames by hand)
  started walks before the grid was ready.

took clicks, one inside Panels didn't.

bot game: a click on the Inventory tab switches to it, one on the X closes it. Test:
test_play.test_ship_computer_layer_processes.

  `tile_gg_*_b` (GAS_SHEET, GAS_SHEET_2 in tools/extract_sprites.py): 96 sprites.

  decks for terrain kinds, hazard-bordered deck by the edges; `"sky": true` - its water is open air with
  nothing drawn (`pc()` returns "" for an empty role; `ground_pieces` and `_tile_cells` skip those); `"alts"`: a
  role's second-sheet drawing used for about half the tiles (`ground_piece`, by a hash of the noise). The

  back edge over the sky gets a rim.

  landing site's patch guaranteed, the map's rim open. In tiled mode the islands are then linked by causeways
  (bridges, 3 tiles wide) in passes - each links the patches within MAX_CAUSEWAY (60 tiles) of the land
  reached so far, re-deriving the terrain types after each pass (the carving sets heights only; without that
  every bridge still counted as sky and the whole planet beyond the pad was filled in as unreachable rock).
  Kronos: 80,477 land tiles, 2 filled.

  depots (containers, barrels, a robot) and relay stations (antenna, radar, beacon) - each on a plot levelled
  flat (its cells in _plot_cells: no stray scenery), at least 22 tiles apart, placed with the chunks' scenery
  (`_industry_in`), either sheet's drawing by a hash. Pirate bands and teleport gates stay.
- Background: `shaders/gas_sky.gdshader`, banded warm clouds drifting slowly (pdata "sky_color") - a placeholder
  until the painted one.

## 2026-11-11 - Beasts that froze mid-lunge; volcanic beasts 4x as tough
- Asked: some creatures get stuck in the attack animation without attacking or doing damage; volcanic
  creatures should have 4 times larger health.
- Cause: SurfaceCreature._fight bit only when the prey was in reach AND the predator stood at its own side of
  it (each pack member closes in from its own side); a charger in reach whose side was blocked kept trying to
  step there, failed, and stayed in its charging (act) pose - never biting - until it gave up (4 s) and came
  back. Now: in reach, it bites wherever it stands; its side blocked, it goes straight at the prey; no step at
  all, it stands (pose 0) instead of freezing mid-lunge.
- SurfaceCreature.FIERCE_HP = 4: the volcanic beasts have 4 times their "like"'s health (FIERCE 2 stays for the
  bite): the magma behemoth and fumarole titan 560, the vent crab 520, the basalt golem 480, the rest 160-220.
- Docs: game.md. Tests: test_volcanic.test_volcanic_beasts_are_tougher (4x health, 2x bite),
  test_a_beast_in_reach_bites (a vent crab and a cinder stalker in reach on the far side of their spot bite at
  once). Files: scripts/surface_creature.gd; data/docs/game.md; tests/test_volcanic.gd.

## 2026-11-11 - Drag and drop: toolbar and inventory slots
- Asked: allow dragging and dropping an item from one toolbar slot to another, and the same for inventory
  slots.
- ItemSlot: drag and drop (payload: what dragging it carries; on_drop / accepts: what a drop on it does);
  a click is now a press and release without a drag (so a drag never clicks).
- Inventory slot layouts: Inventory.slots(inv, layout, cap) - every slot [id, count] or empty: an item's
  stacks fill the slots the layout gives it first, what's new goes to the first empty slots, slots of items
  gone empty; swap(layout, a, b); move_stack_into (a drop across: into that slot if free). Saved per player:
  layout_hold, layout_carried (PlayerData and the surface's player state).
- Toolbars (the bottom bars in space and on foot, and the inventory pages' rows): drag a slot onto another -
  they swap; drag something usable onto a slot - a weapon / system row or repair kits (Ship Computer), your
  rifle / medicine / an energy cell (Field Computer) - it goes there (and leaves its old slot)
  (Inventory.toolbar_drop / toolbar_accepts). Clicking a bottom-bar slot fires on release now.
- Grids: the Ship Computer's hold and what you carry (drag to arrange; between them, a stack moves), the
  Field Computer's carried slots (arrange; drag onto the toolbar), the transfer screen at your ship (arrange
  each side; drag across - the stack moves into that slot).
- Help lines, docs (game.md). Test: test_inventory.test_drag_and_drop (layouts, swaps, a drop across into a
  slot, toolbar swaps and drops, what's refused, a slot's drag / drop). 165 passed. Checked in a bot run
  with real mouse events: a hold stack dragged from slot 1 to 6 (the icon follows the mouse), the laser
  dragged from the weapons list onto toolbar slot 8.

## 2026-11-11 - 120 FPS everywhere: the frame-rate tour, and what it found
- Asked: run or make tests to make sure the game runs at 120 FPS in all areas and ways of gameplay (then, once
  that holds, try for 240 - or say what it would take).
- The test: tests/fps_tour.gd + tools/fps_test.py - plays every area in a real window (vsync off, no frame
  cap; muted, upper-left), a few seconds each, and fails a scenario under 120 FPS (average, and 95% of its
  frames <= 8.33 ms): title; space at home and in every empire (idle, flying, a 6-pirate battle, the
  Minotaur, every Ship Computer tab, every station tab), every signal-site kind, the landing, and every
  landable planet (idle, a long walk streaming the world in, a fight with a pack, inside a building, the
  Field Computer's inventory and map, the transfer screen) - 65 scenarios. Options: a filter, --target=N, --shots
  (a screenshot each), --profile (Godot's script profiler through external/live_debugger/profiler.gd: each
  scenario's functions by their time, its slow frames' and its >24 ms frames' own lists), --attrib, --res.
  Own user data (never the user's). Not in tools/test.py (headless: nothing rendered).
- First run (RTX 2070 Super, 1920x1080): 24 of 25 space scenarios under 120 - flying 57-77 FPS, the battle
  25, Ship Computer 61-86, stations 53-88; surfaces 105-168.
- Fixes, biggest first:
  - Engine trails drew hundreds of anti-aliased circles a frame (545 in a battle: 7 ms): the puffs are now one
    baked disc texture (ExhaustTrail.disc(), batched), the trail's points worked out once a frame (shared by
    the cloud and its glow), 12 px apart instead of 9. Flying 57 -> 250 FPS, the battle 25 -> 140-190.
  - Full-screen menus (Ship Computer, station window, Field Computer) drew the whole world behind them every
    frame: now the world is a picture taken as the menu opens (MenuBackdrop, new) and isn't drawn while it's
    open - the game goes on, a hit still closes the menu. Station tabs 60-150 -> 460-840 FPS, Ship Computer
    -> 330-630, Field Computer 105-140 -> 280-470.
  - Walkability (hundreds of checks a frame by the animals): the buildings in a 512 px grid
    (PlanetSurface._index_buildings) and, inside one, its walls / columns / furniture in a 48 px grid
    (_clear_in) - test_walkable_index_matches_the_full_check (2 planets, thousands of points: the same answers).
  - Animals: the far ones (every 4th frame) each in its own phase (all of them updated in the same frame
    before: a spike every 4th frame); off screen, every other frame; redrawn only in view.
  - Shadows (dozens a frame) from the baked disc; the deathtrap field's hazards only on screen, from the disc
    (98 -> 276 FPS); the galaxy map: its fit worked out once (was 130 times a frame), the still parts
    (grid, stars, territories, peaceful lanes) and the badges / names in layers redrawn only on change
    (77 -> 350 FPS); orbit rings redrawn only when a moon's centre moves; the radar at 30 Hz; portraits at 30 Hz;
    SpaceStation.protecting reads the stations list once a frame; idle ships look for a target every 0.4 s
    (not every frame - creatures still do: they hunt you); the Field Computer's inventory rebuilt only when
    what's in it changes; fog-of-war texels kept up to date as cells are revealed (no full rebuild loop).
  - Landing: the planet scene stays loaded from the loading screen on (ProcArt.scenes) - the first landing
    no longer freezes 0.4 s as you click Land; the ground tile layers built one a frame; the build's slices
    3 ms while the landing plays (6 before); the stair-spot search skips a spot at its first failed test.
    The scene switch's first frame (~270 ms: drawing the whole tiled ground the first time) is under the
    black fade - reported by the tour as info, not a stutter.
  - The trail's glow: its three lightning streaks in one pass, jags from a cheap hash (no RandomNumberGenerator
    per point), each point's cloud width worked out once (was six times).
- Result (last full run): 65 of 65 scenarios at 120+, 166 tests pass. Idle space ~345 FPS, flying 230-450,
  battle 157-166 (worst place in the tour), menus 330-840, planets: idle 183-530, walking 172-500, fights
  152-275, landing animation ~330. The tour's summary also counts the 240 bar (--target=N to judge by
  another): 25 of 65 short of 240 - Thalassa / Krystallos / Selene (all their scenarios), the space battle,
  the Minotaur, flying in some systems, 3 signal sites.
- Files: tests/fps_tour.gd, tools/fps_test.py, external/live_debugger/profiler.gd (new); scripts/menu_backdrop.gd
  (new), exhaust_trail.gd, surface_props.gd, surface_creature.gd, planet_surface.gd, building_floors.gd,
  fog_of_war.gd, pages/galaxy_page.gd, pages/field_inventory_page.gd, orbit_rings.gd, minimap.gd, station.gd,
  portrait.gd, signal_site.gd, enemy.gd, main.gd, proc_art.gd, loading_screen.gd; tests/test_surface.gd.

## 2026-11-11 - 240 FPS everywhere (and kept there)
- Asked: push it to 240 FPS minimum for the whole game (after 120), keep working until it's achieved, and
  create the benchmarks and tests that keep it so in the future.
- Result (RTX 2070 Super, 1920x1080): all 65 scenarios of the tour at 240+ (average and 95% of frames),
  no frame over 50 ms; the slowest (last run, saved as the baseline): a pack fight on Amnissos 365 FPS,
  the Minotaur 430, a space battle 433 (p95 3.1 ms), Amnissos idle 434, the missions tab 438. Planets that were 150-230 now 450-1300 (Kamares 160 -> 830,
  Akrotiri 1200, Dikte 1300). 173 tests pass.
- What it took:
  - Batching: a planet's ground pieces in one atlas texture (TerrainTiles.tile_set: one TileSetAtlasSource
    region each, texture padding off - Godot's padding made each source its own texture again); every
    building wall / floor / roof / sprite piece in one atlas after the loading screen composes them
    (MinoanTiles._atlased; TextureAtlas.pack - new: rows, each image with 3 px of its own edge pixels round it).
    Draw calls on Amnissos 1160 -> ~330.
  - The ground drawn as pictures (GroundChunks, new): the tile layers (up to 22 layers, tens of thousands of
    tiles - ~1.5 ms of CPU a frame even batched) live in a world of their own; 1024 px squares of it are
    rendered once each into small off-screen viewports as they come near the view (2 a frame; all at once
    after landing / a teleport / respawn); those are shown. Pixel-identical to the tiles (a diff: 526 of 2M
    pixels, animations); as sharp zoomed in. GroundChunks.enabled = false: the tiles live again.
  - Far culling (PlanetSurface._cull_far): scenery, building pieces, furniture well off screen go on a
    visibility layer the viewport doesn't draw (filed by 512 px squares; only squares entering / leaving
    view change) - Godot skips them when gathering and y-sorting; animals and people by position.
  - Menus: MenuBackdrop now hides the world by that visibility-layer trick (not `visible = false`: showing
    a planet again redrew every piece of scenery and rebuilt the ground - a 150 ms frame when a bite closed
    the Field Computer); the layers below the menu (space's starfield, the HUD) hidden.
  - Throttled redraws (UI.redraw_due, new: at most N a second, each node its own phase): the engine trails'
    cloud and streaks (60 Hz; the plume at the nozzle every frame, its own node), stations, teleport gates,
    quest bulbs, the landing pad, both toolbars (30 Hz), pickups, monster orbs, mining beams, the system map.
    (The screen shows 60 a second anyway.)
  - Less per-frame work: animals off screen every 4th frame, far ones every 8th; ships off screen every other
    frame; doors off screen every 8th; guards look for a foe every 0.15 s; wall fading every other frame;
    lifts only for what's in view; the occluders loop skips the far ones; stroll checks 8 px apart; the
    galaxy's economy tick spread over frames (6 stations a frame) and one trader departure a frame; ships'
    separation list once a frame; the Esc menu's title not redrawn while hidden; monster orbs and the plume
    from the baked disc; the planet's fog texture no longer resized 4x on each update; a trail's points in
    packed arrays (were a dictionary each: most of a trail's cost), its cloud's colours worked out once a
    point, its three streaks in one pass.
  - Loading without stutters: flat ground layers added in strips of 3000 tiles a frame; buildings raised a
    step a frame (shell; stairs + upper floor; furniture; upstairs) - while loading and as you walk near
    (a 25-45 ms frame each before); people spawned 2 a frame; the stairs search remembers each pair of cells;
    the props atlas's mipmaps on a worker thread; every character sheet's frames worked out on the loading
    screen (SheetPuppet.warm). The landing animation: 8 frames of 25-68 ms -> one of ~26-30 ms.
- Kept so: tools/fps_test.py now judges against 240 by default, fails a frame over 50 ms, and compares with
  tests/fps_baseline.json (new; --save-baseline) - a scenario under 3/4 of its baseline (and under 480 FPS)
  fails. tests/test_frame_budget.gd (new, in the normal suite): the ground's and buildings' pieces share one
  atlas, the ground is drawn as pictures, far culling, throttled redraws, and a script budget a frame on a
  planet and in a battle (4 ms; ~1 now). CLAUDE.md: a "Frame rate: 240 FPS minimum" section.
- Files: scripts/ground_chunks.gd, texture_atlas.gd (new); terrain_tiles.gd, minoan_tiles.gd, planet_surface.gd,
  menu_backdrop.gd, ui.gd, exhaust_trail.gd, enemy.gd, main.gd, galaxy.gd, station.gd, toolbar.gd,
  surface_toolbar.gd, surface_creature.gd, surface_props.gd, sliding_door.gd, teleport_gate.gd, quest_bulb.gd,
  pickup.gd, space_monster.gd, mining_beam.gd, pages/map_page.gd, retro_title.gd, building_floors.gd,
  sheet_puppet.gd, proc_art.gd; tests/fps_tour.gd, test_frame_budget.gd (new), fps_baseline.json (new),
  test_surface.gd, test_gas_giant.gd; tools/fps_test.py; external/live_debugger/profiler.gd; CLAUDE.md.

## 2026-11-11 - Quad cores: background work kept to a share of the machine
- Asked: can the game run smoothly on a quad core? A first run on 4 of this machine's cores (taskset): frame
  rates held (slowest ~380 FPS), but streaming the world in stuttered - the landing 11 frames of 30-95 ms,
  single 56-98 ms frames walking on a planet: the path grid's build on worker threads (every wall of every
  building tested for each of its points, on as many threads as the engine allows) starved the game's own
  thread of time. Asked to fix it.
- Done: the path grid's workers use the same fast walkability as the game (_snapshot_index: the buildings
  by square with their fine grids, made on the main thread, read by the workers - _walkable_snap; a test
  checks it agrees with the full check everywhere); background work capped at a quarter of the machine's
  threads, at least one (BgWork, new: the path grid's group tasks, scenery chunks planted at a time);
  tools/fps_test.py --cores N: the game on N of this machine's cores, told it has N (user arg --cores=N).
  173 tests pass.
- Result, as a quad core (4 of the Ryzen 3900X's cores, no SMT, the desktop sharing them): all 65 scenarios
  at 240+ (two full runs); slowest the Amnissos pack fight ~350 FPS, the Minotaur ~380, a space battle
  330-440 (p95 3.3-4.2 ms - at the bar's edge in one run of four); the landing animation 11 frames of
  30-95 ms -> one of 26 ms; no walking stalls (were 56-98 ms). (A run while another game used ~8 cores
  fell far short everywhere - a busy machine is a slower one.)
- Tried: Godot's separate rendering thread (--render-thread separate) - engine errors (screen read-backs,
  render-thread-only calls) and no gain; left at the default. tools/fps_test.py --render-thread to try it.
- Files: scripts/bg_work.gd (new), planet_surface.gd; tools/fps_test.py; tests/test_surface.gd.
